head: b905f97
evidence: NOT IMPLEMENTED. Scoped, measured and de-risked; the rule is not written and no corpus was rebuilt. What was established: MECHANISM - the driver's FM program entries are (lo, hi, run); a SCALED (pitch-proportional vibrato) entry is marked by hi in $40-$43, so a real Hz delta landing there is read as a vibrato leg and silently lost. flush() in bin/build_mon_native_song.py already clamps byte2 (run) to $01-$7e because $7f=LOOP and $80+=SEMITONE, but there is NO equivalent guard on byte1 - the same class of dispatch collision, guarded in one byte and not the other. MEASUREMENT (new, behaviour-neutral probe FM_SCALE_PROBE=1 added at flush(), the single choke point every entry passes through): DMC Balloon 123,180 collisions, hi byte exactly $41, voices 0 and 2 - matches the documented +16833 = $41C1 two-octave arp and the voice that went 80.6 -> 100.0 when the marker was disabled, so the probe reproduces the known defect as a positive control. HardTrack Love_tune_2 1,096 collisions, hi $41/$42/$43, all three voices (the documented $4300 drum delta). DMC Depeche_Mode_Songs 0. DMC Spy_vs_Spy_III 0. CONCLUSION - the collision is a property of the SONG's own deltas, never the player. no_fm_scale=1 is NECESSARY for the colliding songs and OVER-BROAD for the rest of the corpus, which is exactly the defect the task names, now with numbers instead of an argument.
verify_output: NOT RUN - verify is 'Hubbard, HardTrack and DMC corpora rebuild with no shim opt-out and no regression vs current medians'. No corpus was rebuilt. The DMC corpus alone took ~65 min (16:09-17:14 on 2026-08-15), so all three plus the median comparison is the bulk of the remaining work and was not attempted.
notes: DESIGN OBSTACLE NOT IN THE TASK DESCRIPTION, and it makes the naive implementation UNSOUND: the scaled-substitution decision at build_mon_native_song.py:1668 is taken PER NOTE, during the same pass that fills the collision set, so at that moment the set is still incomplete. A 'check the set' implementation decides on partial information. The sound shape is a PRE-SCAN: compute the plain per-note deltas for the whole song, decide FM_SCALED once, then run the emit pass. The fixed point is well-defined because substitution only replaces a plain program with an exactly-equivalent scaled one (guarded by _fm_unroll equality) and so never creates new plain deltas - but the ordering must be corrected or the rule is wrong. KEEP hard_restart SEPARATE in a first cut: it currently implies the opt-out for Hubbard for the same collision reason, but retiring that implication changes Hubbard too and should be a second step with its own rebuild. UNCOMMITTED CHANGE LEFT IN THE TREE: bin/build_mon_native_song.py carries the FM_SCALE_PROBE diagnostic (a module-level flag, an accumulator, an atexit reporter, and a 5-line observation inside flush()). It is byte-neutral by construction - the emitted tuple is unchanged, hi is the same expression hoisted to a local, and the accumulator only fills when the env var is set. It is the measurement instrument for the remaining work; revert it if that work is not taken up. RUNNER GAP: this outcome is recorded 'inconclusive' because the schema has no value for 'real progress, not finished'. done/failed/inconclusive/blocked cannot express a partial. See opened id runner-partial-outcome.

head: b905f97
evidence: passband_check --player dmc --files Soap_Theme: 'LP+BP' vs 'off/LP+BP', oChg 0, dChg 1, off 8, agree 99.1, routed 73%, window [26s = its own part 1] (matches the .span sidecar '0 26', so not an F8 over-run). CAUSE: a STARTUP TRANSIENT - the native driver has no $D418 default at INIT. At true offset 0 there are exactly 19 mismatching frames, contiguous, frames 0-18 (0.38s), every one orig=LP+BP / ours=off, and ZERO mismatches in the remaining 1280 frames. The original's mode sequence has 0 transitions - LP+BP is already set on the first captured frame, i.e. at song INIT - while ours has exactly 1 transition, off -> LP+BP at frame 19, after which the two agree byte-for-byte to the end of the window. The other three shapes are ruled out: not a LAG (the original never modulates again, so there is no recurring event to be late against), not a WRONG MODE (we select the original's exact LP+BP, just late), not MISSING MODULATION (the original does not modulate at all here). INAUDIBLE on direct evidence: $D417 routing is 0 on all 19 mismatching frames, so the passband is selecting among outputs nothing is fed to. 13 other DMC files show the identical driver shape (ours 'off/X', dChg 1) and score 100.0 only because their originals also start at 'off' - Soap_Theme is the one file whose original sets a non-off passband at INIT, which is what exposes the driver gap.
verify_output: PASS - 'passband_check --player dmc reports the mismatching frames and their cause'. Frames named (0-18 at offset 0), cause named (no INIT-time $D418 default), audibility settled by the routing register rather than asserted.
notes: TOOL DEFECT FOUND AND INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED - compare()'s fitted offset is a curve-fitting artifact. I re-ran the fit myself with the tool's own _agree_at: for Soap_Theme the match count ok is FLAT AT 1280 for every offset >= 0, while n shrinks 1299 -> 1291, so the rate climbs monotonically 98.537% -> 99.148% and off=8 (== max(OFFSETS), the search boundary) wins having bought +0.611 pp with EXACTLY ZERO extra matches. compare() maximises c[1]/c[2], the RATE; its only guard (n >= widest*0.5) is documented in the source as never binding at these offsets. _agree_at trims the TAIL while the mismatches sit at the HEAD, so the shift cannot fix them. THIS FLIPPED A VERDICT: Soap_Theme is reported 99.1% and counted a PASS against --min 99.0, but is 98.537% unshifted, which would FAIL. The compare() docstring instructs the reader to treat a large offset as a real finding ('the passband is right but arrives late') - here it measures nothing of the kind. Fix shape: a shift may only win if it strictly INCREASES ok; ties go to offset 0. See opened id passband-offset-fit-degenerate.

head: b905f97
evidence: passband_check --player sdi --files Arabia: original 'BP/LP+BP/LP+BP+HP' vs ours 'BP/LP+BP', oChg 2, dChg 1, off 4, agree 98.2, routed 23%/3a, '<== mode mismatch', window [18s = its own part 1] (matches the .span '0 18', so F8 ruled out). CAUSE: UNANCHORED DRIVES - SDI's native filter dispatch is gate/note-anchored only. The original runs a continuous per-frame cutoff sweep (1640 -> 1616) plus two passband changes (BP -> LP+BP+HP at frame 688 -> LP+BP at 704) starting 20 frames BEFORE the voice's next gate event, and routes voice 3 in at frame 701, 7 frames before that gate. Our build holds $D416/$D417/$D418 completely static (cutoff pinned 1200, filtctl 0xf0, mode BP) across that whole pre-onset window and writes the new filter state only at the frame the next note is dispatched (708), where it then matches exactly. Ruled out with direct evidence: NOT a lag (the anchor events - gate-off at 706, gate-on at 708 with freq 2649/2650 - land on byte-identical frame numbers on both sides); NOT a wrong mode (we never select a passband the original does not use); NOT missing modulation (we do modulate BP -> LP+BP, just late and without the intermediate LP+BP+HP); NOT F9 (the original's cutoff is actively swept 1640->1616, never held at 0); NOT the b905f97 canonical-key collapse (consistent with Arabia surviving that rebuild unchanged - this is a WHEN-do-we-write defect, not a WHICH-program-did-we-pick defect). AUDIBILITY: of 20 mismatching frames at offset 0 (687-706, contiguous), 13 are inaudible (filtctl low nibble 0, nothing routed) and 7 are audible (voice 3 routed at filtctl 0x84 while we are still BP with nothing routed) - 7 frames, 140 ms, one pre-note filter gesture on one voice, in an 899-frame window.
verify_output: PASS - 'passband_check reports the mismatching frames; cause named or escalated'. Cause named (gate-anchored filter dispatch missing the original's between-note automation), with all four alternative shapes eliminated by register-level evidence rather than by elimination-by-assertion.
notes: SECOND, INDEPENDENT SIGHTING OF THE compare() OFFSET DEFECT, on a different player and a different mismatch shape - which is what raises it from a quirk to a tool bug. I reproduced the fit: at off=0 ok=879/899, and at the fitted off=4 ok is STILL 879, of 895 - the winning shift buys +0.437 pp with ZERO extra matches, and ok then FALLS (878, 877, 876, 875) at offsets 5-8. Arabia generalises the Soap_Theme case: its mismatch block is MID-SONG (frames 687-706), not a head transient, so the defect is not limited to startup - any contiguous mismatch block outside the trimmed tail lets a positive shift inflate the rate for free. IT ALSO CORRUPTS THE AUDIBLE COUNT: the tool reports audible=3 because it counts on the disagreeing frames AT THE FITTED OFFSET; the true count at offset 0 is 7. So the offset artifact propagates into the one column that decides whether a residual matters. Both files' fitted offsets gain exactly zero extra matches - that is the signature to test for.

head: 00893cd
evidence: passband_check --player hardtrack --files Fun_Factory: LP/LP+BP both sides, oChg 12, dChg 12, off -3, agree 99.0, routed 93%/3a, '<== mode mismatch', window [6s = its own part 1] (matches the .span '0 6'). This file DOES exercise $D418 (12 mode changes each side, routed 93%), so it is on the scored side of the 10-of-33 line, not withheld. EXACTLY 3 mismatching frames, orig idx 264-266, orig=LP / ours=LP+BP, n=296. CAUSE: 11 of the 12 transition pairs sit at a constant -3 (this file's documented render offset); the 12th (LP->LP+BP at orig 267) is early by -6, an EXTRA 3-frame advance on top of the normal offset, and the block back to LP returns to -3 - so only that block's onset is early and our block runs 9 frames against the original's 6. In the register trace the original enters the passband change only at the GROUP hard restart (all three voices hit the test-bit reset together at f267); our voice 1 fires an ISOLATED wf test-bit blip 3 frames earlier with adsr unchanged (0x6aa), not shared by voices 0/2, and that spurious note-on re-arms the global filter early. _arm_filter (sidm2/hardtrack_synth.py:475-498) keeps $D418 mode as single-instance state re-seeded from field 12 of whichever voice triggers last, so one premature voice-1 trigger is sufficient. SR_PREKILL RULED OUT by reading the ASM: drivers_src/mon/romuzak_driver.asm:1896-1943 writes SID+6,y ($D406) only and never touches $D417/$D418.
verify_output: PASS - 'passband_check reports the 3 frames and their cause'. The 3-frame figure held exactly and needed no revision. Headline independently corroborated by my own corpus sweep, where Fun_Factory is the sole HardTrack failure at 99.0% (32/33). The transition-offset table and register walk are the agent's own work, internally consistent but not re-derived by me.
notes: AUDIBLE, unlike the other two passband residuals closed today: all 3 frames have filtctl 0xf2 (voice 1 routed) with voice 1's gate open on both sides, and the tool's own audible=3 agrees. The agent DECLINED to force-fit the five named buckets and reported it as its own shape - correct call. It is note-anchored (unlike Arabia's unanchored drives) but anchored to a spurious note-on; it is not a uniform lag, since 11 of 12 transitions already match the fitted -3. NOT ROOT-CAUSED: what makes voice 1 reach `trigger` 3 frames early at this one row is unsettled. The agent named what would settle it - a wf/freq diff over the same window to confirm the desync is isolated to voice 1, or a RetroDebugger trace of the row-dispatch/duration logic - and ran neither, per the measurement-only scope. SIDE NOTE, useful for the offset-fit fix: this file's off=-3 is a REAL negative offset that earns its matches, and it survived 00893cd unchanged - evidence the fix did not flatten legitimate alignments.

head: 00893cd
evidence: IMPLEMENTED AND VALIDATED, NOT YET ADOPTED. `_fm_would_collide(m, frames, delay)` in bin/build_mon_native_song.py decides the $40-$43 SCALED-marker question per SONG, and build_native_song caches the verdict on m BEFORE the emit pass - which is the whole point, since the substitution is chosen per note inside that pass and would otherwise read a set still filling. THE SCAN IS CHEAP BECAUSE OF AN IDENTITY: for k>=2, delta[k] = (freq[k]-base)-(freq[k-1]-base) = freq[k]-freq[k-1] - the base CANCELS - so every within-note delta is a plain consecutive-frame difference, independent of how the song is cut into notes or clipped into windows. Only delta[1] is base-relative, covered by an unwindowed m.voices walk. The scanned set is therefore a strict SUPERSET of what is emitted: it can over-report (falling back to today's behaviour, costing an optimisation) but can never under-report, which is what would ship the defect. VALIDATED 4/4 ACROSS 2 PLAYERS against the e731046 probe counts: DMC Balloon collide=True (probe 123,180), HardTrack Love_tune_2 collide=True (probe 1,096), DMC Depeche_Mode_Songs collide=False (probe 0), DMC Spy_vs_Spy_III collide=False (probe 0). STAGED: default is today's rule verbatim (byte-identical builds); FM_SCALE_AUTO=1 is the measured rule alone. The AUTO path was exercised end-to-end on Spy_vs_Spy_III - scale_ok=True despite the shim's no_fm_scale=1, i.e. the marker comes back for a non-colliding song, and the build completes. 4 unit tests pin the identity synthetically (marker hit, clear song, segmentation-invariance, and the siddump-gap hold that a naive None subtraction would turn into a huge fake delta). 110 tests pass across the 8 suites covering the module.
verify_output: NOT RUN - verify is 'Hubbard, HardTrack and DMC corpora rebuild with no shim opt-out and no regression vs current medians'. No corpus was rebuilt. That is the remaining work: run all three under FM_SCALE_AUTO=1 and compare medians, then flip the default and retire the shim flags.
notes: A STAGING ERROR I MADE AND CORRECTED MID-TASK, worth carrying: the first cut let the measured verdict ADD a disable in default mode and I described that as byte-neutral. It is not. No MoN / SDI / FC / Sound Monitor shim sets no_fm_scale, so a colliding song under one of those would have changed behaviour with no corpus evidence - the right fix, but shipped unverified. The default is now today's rule verbatim and the entire new rule sits behind FM_SCALE_AUTO. Caught by reading the validation output's own scale_ok column, not by reasoning about the diff. hard_restart KEPT SEPARATE in both modes, as planned - retiring its implication changes Hubbard and deserves its own rebuild. SECOND CONSECUTIVE 'inconclusive' FOR THIS TASK, and the two mean different things: the first was 'measured, nothing built', this is 'implemented, validated, not adopted'. The schema cannot tell them apart, which is exactly the case runner-partial-outcome names - this is now its second data point. UNCOMMITTED: bin/build_mon_native_song.py (the scan + wiring), pyscript/test_dmc_native_song.py (4 tests), pyscript/passband_check.py (the retraction comment from the offset-fit work).

Its 'read the LAST line per id' rule is intact.

head: 4d44f00
evidence: passband_check --player sdi --files Funk_Facet: original LP/LP+HP vs ours LP/LP+HP, oChg 115, dChg 115, off 0, agree 99.0, routed 100%/12a, '<== mode mismatch', window [24s = its own part 1]. 12 mismatching frames at indices 107,203,299,...,1163 - a PERFECTLY REGULAR 96-frame period (~1.92s), i.e. one riff repeating 12 times across the window. Every one is byte-identical in shape: orig 0x50 (LP+HP) vs ours 0x10 (LP), and only that pair occurs. CAUSE: UNANCHORED DRIVES, the same bucket as SDI Arabia and the same player. At each site the original writes the new $D418 mode on the frame BEFORE the note onset - its filter automation steps on its own clock, independent of the gate - while our dispatch writes the mode only on the onset frame itself, so we are exactly one frame late and re-sync on the very next frame. Differs from Arabia only in degree: there the pre-onset write is dropped entirely, here it survives one frame late. AUDIBLE 12/12: every mismatch frame has $D417 low nibble 1 (voice 0 routed) with the gate open (wf 0x40/0x41, mid-sustain). The agent's independent count agrees with the tool's printed 12a. Ruled out with evidence: not a startup transient (12 events spread across the window, not one at boot); not a spurious early note-on (wrong direction - we are late, not early); not missing modulation (oChg == dChg == 115, we modulate exactly as often as the original).
verify_output: PASS - 'passband_check --player sdi --files Funk_Facet reports its post-00893cd number, frames and cause'. I re-derived every headline figure independently through the tool's own API rather than trusting the report: pct=98.99917 (rounds to 99.0), n=1199, oChg=dChg=115, off=0, 12 mismatches with inter-gap set {96} exactly, mode pairs {(0x50, 0x10)} exactly, and best-by-match-count offset = 0 with ok=1187/1199. All match.
notes: THE NUMBER DID NOT MOVE, contrary to my expectation when I framed the task. I briefed the agent that the recorded 99.0% and 12 audible frames PREDATE 00893cd and were therefore suspect, because the old rate-maximising fit had inflated Soap_Theme and corrupted Arabia's audible count from 7 to 3. For this file both figures are unchanged, and the agent explained why rather than just reporting it: the old fit only paid when disagreement clustered near the trimmed TAIL, and here the 12 events are spread evenly at 96-frame intervals, so no shift ever bought a match. My own check confirms it - best-by-count offset is 0. So 'predates the fix' is a reason to RE-MEASURE, not a reason to expect movement, and this file is a clean control showing 00893cd left an already-correct fit alone. THIRD FILE IN THE UNANCHORED-DRIVES FAMILY and the SECOND in SDI, which strengthens the case that sdi-filter-between-note-automation is one root cause rather than per-file defects: Arabia (pre-onset write dropped, 7 audible frames) and Funk_Facet (pre-onset write one frame late, 12 audible frames) are the same mechanism at two severities. Fixing the dispatch should close both; whoever takes that task should verify against BOTH files, not just Arabia. All 12 frames here are AUDIBLE, unlike Arabia where 13 of 20 were inaudible - so this is the more audible of the two despite the higher percentage. Percentage alone would have ranked them the other way round.

head: 6e5daf9
evidence: MECHANISM ESTABLISHED EXACTLY, with a concrete fix identified that needs NO driver change. detect_filter_drives (build_mon_native_song.py:756) credits a filter-envelope attack at frame f to a note-on only when -1 <= (f - onset) <= 4. Measured on Arabia: the attack is at frame 688 (cutoff 448 -> 1640, ctrl 0xf0 -> 0x80); voice-2 gate rises nearby are 603, 609, 637, 708, 718. So the attack sits in a 71-FRAME GAP BETWEEN TWO NOTES - +51 frames after onset 637 and -20 before onset 708 - and is outside the window at both ends, so it is dropped entirely. Nothing is routed at 688 (ctrl 0x80); routing arrives at ~701. SDI's filter genuinely steps on its own clock, unanchored to any gate. That explains both severities in one model: Funk_Facet's write is exactly 1 frame pre-onset, which just scrapes into the -1 bound, so it IS credited but the program is anchored AT the onset and therefore arrives one frame late (12 sites, all audible). Arabia's is 20 frames out, so it is lost completely (7 audible frames of 20). THE FIX THAT FOLLOWS: filter_program_for captures from the onset for `span` frames and a hold is just ADD-0 rows, so crediting the 688 attack to onset 637 would produce 51 frames of hold followed by the real automation - reproduced exactly, inside the existing driver. The change is the mapping window's UPPER bound (currently +4); it needs to reach at least +51 for this file.
verify_output: NOT RUN - verify is 'Arabia frames 687-706 AND Funk_Facet's 12 sites agree, and the SDI passband count does not fall'. Nothing was changed, so nothing was rebuilt. No code edit was made at all; the working tree is clean and the lock is released.
notes: DURABLE, and it is the expensive half: the mechanism is measured rather than hypothesised, both files are explained by ONE model at two severities, and a fix exists that stays inside the current driver. The next attempt starts from 'widen the upper bound and rebuild', not from 'why do these two files differ'. Frame numbers, onsets and the exact code site are recorded above. WHAT REMAINS, and why I stopped rather than starting it: detect_filter_drives is SHARED by six players (the docstring names SM's filter_tie and dynamic-routing paths explicitly), so widening +4 to ~+64 is a behavioural change for all of them, not just SDI. It needs a rebuild-and-compare per player, and SDI alone is 441 files with no --jobs on its sweep. Starting that with the remaining room would have produced a half-verified shared-code change, which is the exact failure this session has spent the day correcting. TWO CAUTIONS FOR THE NEXT ATTEMPT. (1) Verify against BOTH Arabia and Funk_Facet - they are one mechanism at two severities, and a fix that repairs the dropped case could still leave the one-frame-late case, or vice versa. (2) A wider window risks CREDITING AN ATTACK TO THE WRONG NOTE - the -1..+4 bound is what currently keeps a drive attached to the note that caused it, and the docstring records a prior bug (SM Dance part02) where mis-credited attacks collapsed into distinct programs. Check the neighbours, not just the target. NOTHING UNCOMMITTED.

head: 76c0132
evidence: RETRACTION: MY PREVIOUS DIAGNOSIS OF FUNK_FACET WAS WRONG. I recorded that its $D418 write is 1 frame pre-onset, scrapes into the -1 bound, is credited to the note it precedes, and therefore ARRIVES LATE. Measured today at its first mismatch site, that is false. Sequence index 107 = siddump frame 108. At frame 108 the CUTOFF IS UNCHANGED - 256, delta 0, ctrl 0xf1 - while the $D418 mode changes. detect_filter_drives keys exclusively on cutoff jumps (abs(ftr[f][0]-ftr[f-1][0]) >= FILT_FAST = 64), so it sees NO attack at 108 at all; the first attack is at 109, the onset itself. There was never an attack for the matcher to anchor, early or late. PROVED BY CONSTRUCTION, not by argument: I implemented the anchoring fix my diagnosis implied (FILT_BACKANCHOR - prefer an anchor the attack has already passed, since filter_program_for can only capture from the anchor forward) and A/B'd four ways. Funk_Facet reads 99.0% with 12 audible frames in ALL FOUR configurations. The flag is now removed; its rationale is refuted and a dead default-off flag is worse than none. THE REAL SHAPE IS PATTERNS F9 - a detector keyed on one register blind to the same event in another - and this repo has fixed that exact defect once already in this very function: Juba-Jazz (5c5c357), where the filter was enabled by $D417+$D418 with the cutoff held at 0 and nothing was credited. Funk_Facet is the second instance: the passband moves while the cutoff holds.
verify_output: PARTIAL, unchanged in outcome but not in understanding. Arabia PASSES (100.0%, 0 audible) via FILT_LEAD=64, committed inert at 76c0132. head: 76c0132
evidence: FUNK_FACET NARROWED TO ITS LAST STAGE BY ELIMINATION. Three hypotheses tested and REFUTED BY CONSTRUCTION, each by building the fix it implied and measuring: (1) anchoring - FILT_BACKANCHOR, prefer an anchor the attack has passed: no change, 99.0%/12a. (2) detection - FILT_MODEATK, treat a $D418 mode change with the cutoff held as an envelope start, modelled on 5c5c357: no change, 99.0%/12a. Its additive guard (copied from that commit - skip when an earlier pass credited anything within 4 frames) suppresses this case by design, because a drive DOES exist 1 frame away. (3) the whole premise that a drive is missing - MEASURED FALSE. Funk_Facet has 72 drives; near the first mismatch they are at 97, 109, 121. The mode changes 1 -> 5 at frame 108, which the drive at 97 already COVERS. AND THE EMITTED PROGRAM IS CORRECT. filter_program_for(ftr, 97, 12, pbtr) returns 7 rows including a SET row at index 5, (210, 0, 241), at exactly offset 11 = frame 108. The format handles this explicitly ('A passband switch needs a SET row exactly as a res/routing change does'). So detection, anchoring AND program generation are all correct. The loss is DOWNSTREAM of them - canonicalisation, the span the real build passes, or the emit path - not where I have been looking.
verify_output: PARTIAL. Arabia PASSES (100.0%, 0 audible) via FILT_LEAD=64, committed inert at 76c0132. Funk_Facet DOES NOT (99.0%, 12 audible) under every configuration tried: baseline, FILT_BACKANCHOR, FILT_MODEATK, and FILT_LEAD+FILT_MODEATK. 43 tests pass; the working tree is CLEAN - both experimental flags were added, measured and reverted, so HEAD is unchanged.
notes: DURABLE, and it is elimination rather than a fix: the defect is now known NOT to be in the three places I successively believed it was. A drive covering frame 108 exists (97), and the program that drive generates encodes the mode change at the right offset. Whatever discards it happens after filter_program_for returns. WHAT REMAINS: instrument the REAL build rather than calling filter_program_for directly - compare the program actually attached to drive 97 in the emitted artifact against the 7 rows above. The prime suspect is canonicalisation: canon_src keys per-note filter programs and b905f97 had to add the passband to that key for Tanks_3000. If a canonical program without the SET row is substituted here, the symptom matches exactly. Check canon_src/canon_filt for drive 97. THREE WRONG GUESSES IN A ROW ON ONE FILE, and the only reason none of them shipped is that each was A/B'd rather than reasoned about. Two dead flags were written and reverted. The lesson I should have applied sooner: instrument the actual pipeline before hypothesising about which stage is at fault - the measurement that finally narrowed it (dump the drives, then dump the program) cost less than any of the three fixes. SUPERSEDES both earlier records for this id. 'Prefer an EARLIER onset' is wrong. 'The detector is blind to a mode-only change' is true in general but NOT this file's defect. NOTHING UNCOMMITTED.

evidence: The lane gate is replaced by a RESOURCE gate in ~/.claude/commands/runtask.md step 5, and `touches` is redefined in whattask.md step 5. `lane` is now a HINT: contention is computed from `touches`, so a mislabelled lane costs wall-clock and can no longer cost a corrupted run. Four mechanisms: (1) touches declares every shared path READ or WRITTEN, tagged r:/rw: (bare = rw, so the existing plan file stays valid); reader-vs-writer conflicts, reader-vs-reader does not. (2) a tool's SCRATCH file is a write you did not author and must be declared. (3) serial.lock becomes a JSON ARRAY of holder records keyed on touches (a bare object reads as a one-element array), so disjoint serial tasks no longer queue behind each other. (4) the gate consults repo evidence the lockfile cannot see - out/.mon_build.lock and mtimes under every touches path, readers included - because a hand-started rebuild holds no task record. VERIFIED BY A REAL RUN AGAINST LIVE STATE, not a desk-check: ~/.claude/lib/runtask_gate_check.py implements step 5 verbatim and was run while the SDI corpus rebuild was actually in flight. CASE A reader-vs-writer: dmc-stale-artifacts-scored as the plan declares it (touches [], lane parallel) is ALLOWED by the old rule and REFUSED by the new one on out/sdi. CASE B shared scratch: coming-soon-lederhosen vs sdi-unconfirmed-multipart ALLOWED old, REFUSED new on out/sdi/_passband_probe.sid. CASE C unlocked writer, task lock deliberately hidden so only filesystem evidence remains: ALLOWED old, REFUSED new - 'out/sdi (modified 1s ago (Acid_Jazz_native_part01.sid))', which is the live rebuild caught in the act rather than a fixture. notes: CASE C IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN FAKED BY A FIXTURE. out/.mon_build.lock was NOT present at either sampling instant - the build lock is held only for a moment per song - so the mtime sweep is what caught the running rebuild, and a gate relying on the project lock alone would have passed. Both checks are needed; that is why the text names both. Keying the lock on touches fixes that, and the array form is backward compatible so the live holder record written by the in-flight task still reads correctly - I deliberately did NOT migrate or touch another task's lock. Refusing them by hand and then making the gate refuse them automatically is the same act. head: d8a7072
evidence:
All four files (SID/Gallefoss_Glenn/{Culture_Mix_2,Lame,Onkie_Donkie,Culture_Mix_1}.sid) decode as SDIModule variant='D', fpt=3. In bin/build_sdi_native_song.py:402-404 the adaptive/single-window path computes `dec_span = max(e.frame for events) + 100; secs = dec_span//50 + 4`, using sidm2/sdi_parser.py SDIModule.decode_voice(v, max_ticks=40000) (default arg, no override in the build script).

decode_voice for variant D dispatches to _decode_voice_d (sidm2/sdi_parser.py:979-1010), whose only loop bound is `while tick < max_ticks and guard < 4000` (line 990). Its handling of byte $FF (line 993-997, doc'd at 982-983 as "wrap to position 0 = song LOOP") sets `tpos = 0; continue` with NO repeat-count or visited-position guard -- unlike the base/A-variant walk which tracks `seen_loop` (sidm2/sdi_parser.py:677-682) to stop on a second visit to the same loop target. So a D-variant track that ends in a song-loop marker runs until max_ticks is exhausted, period.

Measured with default max_ticks=40000 (all 4 files, 3 voices each):
  Culture_Mix_2: v0 max_frame=119904, v1=119904, v2=119976 -> dec_span=120076 -> dec_span//50=2401
  Lame:          v0=119916, v1=119964, v2=119988          -> dec_span=120088 -> //50=2401
  Onkie_Donkie:  v0=119988, v1=119988, v2=119988          -> dec_span=120088 -> //50=2401
  Culture_Mix_1: v0=119988, v1=119904, v2=119976          -> dec_span=120088 -> //50=2401
floor(dec_span/50)=2401 in all four cases -- this IS the reported "2401s" figure the task names, and it lands there purely because max_ticks(40000)*fpt(3)=120000 is the ceiling being approached, not because of an organic ending near that frame.

Confirmed this is a genuine infinite loop, not four songs that happen to be exactly this long, two ways:
1. Raised max_ticks 10x to 400000 and re-ran decode_voice: in 8 of the 12 voice traces the walk is STILL running against the new ceiling (event count and max_frame both scale ~10x with the cap: e.g. Culture_Mix_2 v1 max_frame 119976->1199976, v2 119976->1199988; Culture_Mix_1 v0 119988->1199976). A song with a real ending would stop producing new events once past its true length regardless of how high the cap goes; these do not.
2. Independently re-walked each voice's track bytes (same $FF/$FE test and tpos+=2 stride as _decode_voice_d, no tick cap at all, just an iteration counter) and counted $FF "wrap to 0" firings: every voice in every file wraps within its first 4-14 track-position entries and then re-wraps every few entries indefinitely -- e.g. Culture_Mix_1 voice0 first wraps at iteration 4 and wraps 5000 times in 20000 manual iterations; Onkie_Donkie's slowest voice still wraps every ~14 iterations (1428-2000 wraps in 20000). None of the 12 voice tracks ever reached the $FE "voice off" stop code in 20000 iterations -- only repeated $FF loop-backs.

Ran (read-only, via python -c sys.path.insert + sidm2.sdi_parser.load_sid/SDIModule, no repo files touched):

2) 10x-cap decode (max_ticks=400000): 8/12 voice traces still climbing at the new ceiling (max_frame scaling ~10x with the cap rather than plateauing) -- e.g. Culture_Mix_2 v1 119976->1199976 frames, v2 119976->1199988; Culture_Mix_1 v0 119988->1199976, v2 119976->1199988.
3) Manual track-byte walk (20000 iterations, no cap): every one of the 12 voice tracks hits its first $FF song-loop marker within 4-14 entries and re-wraps hundreds to thousands of times (1428-5000 wraps counted); zero $FE stop codes seen in any trace.

notes:
Verdict: the "2401s" figure is a CAP, and it is neither of the two DoD-anticipated outcomes cleanly. It is not "genuinely >= the cap, nothing lost" -- there is no finite true song length to be >= anything, because these D-variant tracks are structurally infinite loops (the format's own $FF "song LOOP" marker, decoded per the code's own docstring at sidm2/sdi_parser.py:982-983) and _decode_voice_d has no loop-repeat-count or seen-position guard the way the base/A-variant decode does. It is also not simply "the cap truncates a finite song, name the frame count" in the ordinary sense, because there is no organic ending to name -- raising the cap 10x just moves the truncation point 10x, it does not reveal a real stop. The correct framing: for all 4 files, decode_voice(v) (default max_ticks=40000) is capped by that default, scaled by fpt=3 to a ~120000-frame/2401s ceiling, on tracks that never naturally terminate (no $FE reached, only repeated $FF loop-backs every 4-14 track entries) -- so "song length" is not well-defined for these files under the current decoder, and the round "2401s" seen 3-4 times is exactly the symptom the task title predicted: a cap, not three/four song lengths.

evidence: 13 builds, 3 arms, ALL 4 parts / combined md5 154757d5924b / part sizes 15716,15390,15988,14653: A serial -j1 x5 (43.7-48.1s), B -j8 with ONE file x5 (41.4-42.9s), C -j8 with EIGHT files x3 (215.9/217.6/251.2s). The BEFORE state on disk already read md5 154757d5924b, matching d8a7072's recorded serial artifact byte-for-byte, so this reproduces the historical serial control. TWO HYPOTHESES KILLED WITHOUT SPENDING BUILD TIME. (1) 'the F12 lock was not held': REFUTED by dates -- MON_BUILD_LOCK is set by dmc_native_sweep.py:340 whenever jobs>1, and the lock commit 4d01910 (2026-08-16) is an ancestor of b3d5a40 (2026-08-18), the A/B that produced the 1-part artifact. The lock WAS in force. It guards the shared driver files, not the trace subprocesses. (2) 'span went short': REFUTED by code -- span is max(sum(n.ticks)) over the DECODED voices (build_dmc_native_song.py:429-431), pure arithmetic on the SID bytes, so it cannot vary under load. ROOT CAUSE, identified by code and CONFIRMED by direct test: sidm2/fidelity_common.py:250 run_siddump does subprocess.run(...).stdout with no check=, no returncode inspection, no timeout, stderr discarded. Tested directly: a failing input returns stdout '' (len 0) and siddump_per_frame returns 0 frames with NO exception raised. Bundles are built FROM that trace (build_mon_native_song.py:1449 docstring: 'a COMMAND byte = an (FM, pulse) bundle = the note's per-frame pitch (slide/arp) + PWM from the trace'), and build_song's fits() decides part boundaries purely by comparing those counts to CAP_B/CAP_I/CAP_TBL/CAP_SEG. An empty trace therefore makes the whole song 'fit' -> exactly one part, with rc=0 and no warning. That is the 1-part signature. The trigger is spawn pressure: whats-next.md records that a -j16 build beside other work caused 3 process-launch failures, and the process list during arm C showed concurrent siddump_complete.py spawns, so the pressure is real -- 8 files simply did not reproduce it where 88 did. ASYMMETRY THAT IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT: build_native_song RAISES on a decode that produced no notes (line 1463, 'refusing to build silence -- the decode failed, not the fidelity') but has NO equivalent guard for a trace that came back empty. Blast radius: 17 run_siddump call sites; the trace path is reached by three native builders (mon, sdi, hardtrack). Several SCORERS do guard emptiness (dmc_native_sweep.py:295, passband_check.py:505, validate_filter_accuracy.py:178/244); the BUILDERS do not -- and a builder that does not refuse emits a wrong artifact that then scores clean.

head: dd67bee
evidence:
Measured real traces before setting the bound (clean single run, no other process contention):
  - SID/JohannesBjerregaard/Balloon.sid  -t404 (span+4, the documented long pole, "the best-evidenced number in the project" per docs/players/DMC.md) -> 19.3s wall (0.0478 s wall/s trace)
  - SID/Gallefoss_Glenn/Ghosts_n_Goblins_Arcade.sid -t300 -> 13.9s wall (0.0464 s wall/s trace)
  - SID/Shogoon/Music_Box.sid -t300 -> 4.1s wall (0.0137 s wall/s trace)

Slowest observed rate ~0.048 s wall per s of -t requested. Rather than pin a fixed constant to Balloon's 404s (which the task itself warns against, since trace time scales with -t and a future corpus song could exceed Balloon), the timeout is computed as `_siddump_timeout(args)` = 30.0s floor (interpreter startup + the spawn-contention headroom this module's docstring already documents: 3 real process-launch failures under a -j16 build) + 0.5 * requested_seconds (~10x the slowest measured per-second rate), where requested_seconds is parsed from the `-tN` token in args (falling back to siddump_complete.py's own default of 60s when absent). For Balloon (-t404) this gives a 232.0s budget against a measured 19.3s run — ~12x margin.

subprocess.TimeoutExpired is caught and converted to RuntimeError naming the file, args, and the bound (`f"siddump timed out (>{timeout:.0f}s) on {path} with {list(args)} — ..."`), matching the shape of the existing rc!=0 RuntimeError. The rc!=0 raise and the empty-stdout-on-rc==0 allowance (dd67bee) are both untouched.

notes:
Design choice worth flagging: the bound scales with the `-tN` parsed out of `args` rather than being a single fixed constant, specifically because the task instructions warn that a fixed-seconds bound must clear the worst realistic -t, not just the one tested — and every real builder computes -t dynamically from each song's own length (`secs = span // 50 + 4`), so a future song longer than Balloon is plausible. The parser only recognizes the single-token `-tNNN` form (e.g. `-t404`), which is the only form any real caller in this repo uses (grepped all `run_siddump(` call sites); a caller using a split `-t 404` form would silently fall back to the 60s-equivalent floor rather than erroring — acceptable since no such caller exists today, but worth knowing if one is ever added. The last candidate is the ARPEGGIO pointer table ($1511 -> $1517/$151b/$151f, whose targets read `00 05 09 0c` and `00 04 07 0c` -- chord shapes in semitones), and its pointer HIGH BYTE was being read as a tempo of 21 (Warriors 37) where every decoding file reads 2-5. head: 280b6cc
evidence: IT IS A DEFECT, NOT A DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE -- and the task was to determine which, which a measurement now does. drivers_src/common/sf2_native_driver.asm:393 writes $D418 as `lda F_MODE / ora #$0f / sta SID_VOL`, hardcoding full master volume, while drivers_src/mon/romuzak_driver.asm:477 reads `ora #MAIN_VOL` from layout.inc. MAIN_VOL is emitted by build_romuzak_native_song.py for BOTH paths but appears nowhere in the common file. WHO ACTUALLY USES THE COMMON BODY: both drivers_src/romuzak/romuzak_driver.asm and drivers_src/galway/galway_driver.asm .include it, and B.GAL defaults to drivers_src/romuzak -- only build_mon_native_song.py repoints it at drivers_src/mon, which is why MoN, DMC, Sound Monitor, FC, HardTrack, SDI, Hubbard and Matt Gray all get the MAIN_VOL version and romuzak/galway do not. THE ROMUZAK PATH IS CLEAN: both songs in out/romuzak (Delirious_9_tune_1, Road_of_Excess_end) measure master_volume $F, so the hardcode is harmless there. THE GALWAY PATH IS NOT: over all 40 songs in out/galway_sf2, 39 measure $F and ONE -- MicroProse_Soccer_intro -- measures $C. THE OBVIOUS OBJECTION IS TESTED AND FAILS: for Galway, $D418's low nibble is also the digi carrier, so a modal value could be a sample rather than a volume. It is not. Over 3000 frames (60 s) MicroProse_Soccer_intro holds $C with ONE distinct low-nibble value and no variation whatsoever; the control, Arkanoid, holds $F the same way. A digi carrier does not sit on a single value for 3000 frames. So this is the Supremacy master-volume defect -- the one MAIN_VOL was introduced to fix -- surviving in the second copy, and it renders that tune a quarter louder than the original.

Measurements run: (1) out/romuzak stems -> master_volume $F, $F (2 of 2). (2) out/galway_sf2 stems -> census {'$C': 1, '$F': 39} over 40 songs, sole outlier MicroProse_Soccer_intro. (3) low-nibble distribution over 60 s via siddump_frames_full: MicroProse_Soccer_intro 3000 frames, 1 distinct value, 0xc at 100.0%; Arkanoid 3000 frames, 1 distinct value, 0xf at 100.0%. (4) include graph: galway_driver.asm:23 and romuzak_driver.asm:23 both .include ../common/sf2_native_driver.asm; B.GAL default is drivers_src/romuzak and only bin/build_mon_native_song.py:2437 reassigns it.
notes: NOTHING WAS WRITTEN -- every declared path is r: and the task is a determination, so the FIX is deliberately out of scope and opened as galway-microprose-soccer-renders-a-quarter-loud. That fix would edit drivers_src/common/sf2_native_driver.asm, which is in NO task's touches today, and it changes a driver that assembles into every romuzak and galway build, so it needs its own touches and its own corpus check. SCOPE OF THE HARM, stated rather than rounded up: 1 song of 42 across the two paths that use this driver. The other 41 measure $F, where `ora #$0f` and `ora #MAIN_VOL` are the same instruction. I did not measure whether the digi engine is active on MicroProse_Soccer_intro during the affected frames -- the common driver's DIGI_* paths write SID_VOL themselves at lines 1208+, so the audible size of the error depends on how much of the tune the non-digi write covers, and that is part of the fix task rather than this one. evidence:
PREMISE BUG FOUND AND FIXED in the decision's own instruction. The decision said: 'add a negation after .gitignore:248's `.claude/tasks/` so that whattask.json, interview.json, serial.lock and the session pid file STAY ignored'. Tried that literally first: appended `!.claude/tasks/runs.jsonl` directly after `.claude/tasks/` (a directory-match pattern, trailing slash). This does NOT work -- confirmed via `git check-ignore -v`, which still reported runs.jsonl as ignored by the line-248 rule. This is documented git behaviour, not a fluke: per gitignore(5), 'It is not possible to re-include a file if a parent directory of that file is excluded' -- git never even walks into a directory matched by a trailing-slash pattern, so a negation for a file inside it is silently inert.

FIX: changed `.claude/tasks/` to `.claude/tasks/*` (glob the directory's entries instead of excluding the directory itself) so git still visits the directory and the negation can take effect. head: 0ec8d89
evidence:
Scanned all 33 built HardTrack songs' voice-1 note onsets (siddump_note_onsets from sidm2.fidelity_common) over each file's own part-1 .sf2.span window, original vs built. First pass used a nearest-frame greedy matcher (tol=20 frames): 30/33 songs showed a clean uniform -3 median delta (matching the documented render offset, no deviation); 3/33 (Fun_Factory, Shogoon-Rave, Something_to_Eat) showed a non-(-3) median.

CAUGHT MY OWN METHOD IN THE SAME PITFALL THIS REPO'S OWN E3 FIX ALREADY DOCUMENTS (docs/ROADMAP.md E3: 'a greedy matcher with a window wider than the note spacing can pair an onset with its neighbour'): re-checked Fun_Factory with an order-based (index-paired) alignment instead of nearest-frame -- onset COUNTS DIFFER (48 orig vs 47 built voice-1 onsets), so index-pairing desyncs after the first count mismatch and produces a scattered, unreliable delta distribution ({-3:13, 3:7, 9:6, -9:6, 18:5, 0:4, ...}, all multiples of 3 -- the signature of a cascading misalignment, not 44 independent early events). The nearest-frame matcher's earlier '-6.0 median, n=44' figure for Fun_Factory is THEREFORE ALSO SUSPECT for the same reason (wide tolerance stealing wrong neighbours) and is WITHDRAWN as evidence -- it does not contradict or extend the already-diagnosed root cause (runs.jsonl:passband-fun-factory, an isolated voice-1 wf test-bit blip 3 frames early that re-arms the shared _arm_filter state), which was derived independently by reading the register trace directly, not by onset-counting, and still stands.

Something_to_Eat's 'n=1' outlier is a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT, not a defect: voice 1 has only 2 onsets total in this window on EACH side (orig: B-4@0, A#5@4; built: A#5@1, A#5@501) -- too sparse to say anything, and the note NAMES don't even match between the two paired onsets, confirming the pairing itself is spurious.

SHOGOON-RAVE IS THE ONE CLEAN, TRUSTWORTHY FINDING: orig and built voice-1 onset COUNTS MATCH EXACTLY (253 == 253), so order-based (index-paired) alignment is reliable here with no count-mismatch risk. Result: for onsets 0-246 (of 253) -- i.e. essentially the entire part-1 span (span is [0,24]s = frames 0-1200; the -3-baseline onsets only start at orig frame 1274 = 25.48s, PAST the span) -- voice 1 sits at a consistent delta of +2 (239/253) or +7 (7/253) vs the original, meaning it fires 5 (or 10) frames LATE relative to the render's usual -3 offset, NOT early. This is the OPPOSITE direction from this task's own title ('fires a note-on earlier'), a DIFFERENT song than the one that motivated the task (Fun_Factory), and not previously documented anywhere in this repo. The pattern self-corrects to the normal -3 baseline only after the part-1 window ends (~25.5s onward), which is consistent with a structural cause (e.g. a per-part-boundary counter/tempo resync) rather than a random artifact -- but the actual mechanism needs its own disassembly-level investigation, the same depth of work Fun_Factory's diagnosis took, which is out of scope to redo inline here.

CONCLUSION on this task's own framing: 'voice 1 fires early' is NOT a corpus-wide HardTrack engine behaviour -- ELIMINATED as a general claim. The 30-song '-3 uniform, no deviation' reading from the first pass is directionally believable (a uniform render offset with no drift is the expected, boring case) but not individually re-verified per file with a count-match-safe method, so I am not certifying all 30 as clean, only reporting that nothing in the wide-tolerance pass flagged them. Fun_Factory's ATTRIBUTION stands as already documented (and my attempt to sharpen it further failed safe rather than reporting a wrong sharper number). Shogoon-Rave is a NEW, real, well-evidenced but not-yet-attributed finding -- opened as its own task (hardtrack-shogoon-rave-voice1-late) rather than mis-filed under this task's 'early' framing, since it is a different song, a different direction, and needs its own root-cause dive.

evidence:
Re-ran _probe_sdi over SID/Shogoon: 16 files still confidently claim `sdi` with nothing else in the SIGNATURE set contesting them (the 4 the shape check already catches stay caught). Tried and REFUTED A FOURTH corroboration design, not one of the three whats-next.md already names -- documented so it is not re-derived: byte-pattern REACHABILITY. Hypothesis: locate()'s _find() match is a pure byte-scan with no guarantee the matched bytes are ever executed; if a real SDI file's INIT always runs through its matched offset while a false positive's INIT never reaches its (coincidental) match, that is real signal. Built a py65 PC-trace (traced_run() in the scratch script) recording every visited PC from init_address to the $FFFF sentinel, then checked whether the locate()-matched address was ever visited. RESULT: reached=True for every single one of the 16 Shogoon false positives (n_visited 41-55 instructions each) -- their INIT routines DO execute through the matched byte pattern, because it is a real (if generic) init-copy idiom in THEIR OWN, non-SDI player, not dead/coincidental bytes. Reachability discriminates nothing. (Cross-check note: 3 of 4 Gallefoss_Glenn files sampled as 'known-SDI' controls were actually NOT SDI files at all -- is_sdi_play3 rejected them outright -- a sampling slip on my part, not a finding; corrected by reading is_sdi_play3's own accept/reject rather than assuming every file in that directory is SDI.)

FOUND ONE NEW, PROMISING, NOT-YET-VERIFIED LEAD instead -- structural CLUSTERING by the locate()-matched offset-from-load-address (not absolute address, which varies per song's own load address, but the CONSTANT offset a shared player engine would produce). Computed this for all 16: 13 of them fall into exactly TWO tight clusters --
  offset $0807 (4 files: Bilinski, Dickshake_intro, Kredki, Kredki_end)
  offset $0037 (9 files: Oobat_Noogohs, Part_Preview, Pollena_2000, Technological_Snow, Twilight_of_the_Gods_{end,intro,part_2,part_4,part_5})
and player-id.exe (tools/player-id.exe, run fresh -- not the stale aggregate number) calls ALL 13 of exactly these files 'DMC', independently of the offset clustering. The remaining 3 (Chaos_Note, Nodule, Tekkno) form their own third group -- locate() matches SDI variant D (no A/C offset to cluster by) on all three, AND player-id independently calls all three 'Music_Assembler' (a different, more specific verdict than the generic-and-known-unreliable 'DMC' bucket the module already distrusts).

WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM THE ALREADY-REFUTED 'promote on player-id' DESIGN: that design trusted a SINGLE player-id verdict in isolation and was measured to get 2/6 wrong (75.0%->71.4% precision). This is TWO INDEPENDENT signals converging on the same file groups -- a structural byte-offset fingerprint that recurs identically across multiple unrelated songs (consistent with a shared compiled player engine, which coincidence would not reproduce this tightly) PLUS player-id agreeing for exactly those files. Multi-source convergence is a different evidentiary shape than single-source trust, even though both ultimately cite player-id.

DID NOT SHIP A CODE CHANGE on this lead. Acting on it means either (a) hard-coding these specific two offsets as a downgrade rule (risks overfitting to one 16-file sample and doesn't generalise), or (b) building real corpus-wide fingerprint clustering into native_dispatch.py (comparing every candidate's offset against a reference table built from all 160 known-genuine Gallefoss_Glenn SDI files) -- a real architecture change that needs verifying it does NOT regress the pinned counts (hardtrack 33, mattgray 13, Gallefoss sdi 160) before it can land, matching this repo's own standing rule that a fix ships only after being measured against the corpora it could break. That measurement is real work, not a quick follow-on, and belongs in its own task rather than being rushed in under this cycle's time budget.
